alerts.reason: Buckle's Q2 net sales fell 3.4% (A) even as its average price per piece rose 2.2% (D), implying roughly 5.5% fewer pieces sold. If that unit decline persists and the price gain fades, net sales could fall at least 5% in Q3 or Q4.

Boston Beer's Q2 net revenue fell 4.0% (A). Shipments fell 6.4% across several declining brands (B), while pricing and lower returns lifted revenue per barrel 2.6% (D). With similar shipment weakness, a one-point smaller gain per barrel would put the quarterly revenue decline near 5%.

Intel's Q2 revenue fell about 0.9% despite 9% growth in client computing, helped by comparison with elevated customer inventories a year earlier (A, B). Lower server demand and Altera customers cutting purchases (C, E) could take the consolidated decline to 5% in Q3 or Q4 if the client growth slows.

Amkor's Q2 net sales were flat because communications growth offset declines elsewhere (A). Elevated customer inventories and weak demand drove first-half declines of 19% in automotive and industrial and 12% in consumer (B). If those pressures persist, slower communications growth could tip quarterly net sales down 5% within two quarters.

ArcBest's Q2 consolidated revenue fell 2.3% (A). Lower Asset-Light freight rates and lower Asset-Based daily tonnage weighed on both businesses (B). Further weakness in rates or tonnage could widen the decline by the 2.7 percentage points needed to cross in Q3 or Q4.

Buckle’s net sales fell 3.43% in Q2 (A) even as average price per piece rose 2.2% (D). That implies roughly 5.5% fewer pieces sold. If unit weakness persists, a smaller price increase could take sales growth back to -5% or lower in Q3 or Q4.

Boston Beer’s Q2 net revenue fell 4.01% (A). Shipments fell 6.4% across several brands (B), while pricing and lower returns lifted revenue per barrel 2.6% (D). With similar shipment weakness, just one percentage point less revenue growth would cross -5% in Q3 or Q4.

Molson Coors’ net sales growth fell from +10.66% in Q1 to -0.44% in Q2. Lower volume and unfavorable currency outweighed favorable pricing and mix (B). A further 4.56-point deterioration would take reported sales growth to -5% in Q3 or Q4.

Lincoln Electric’s net sales improved from -5.59% in Q1 to -3.67% in Q2, but it still reported “softer demand across segments” (A) and lower volumes (C). Only another 1.34 points of deterioration would produce a fresh crossing in Q3 or Q4.

Intel’s total revenue growth fell from +8.61% in Q1 to -0.90% in Q2 despite 9% client computing growth as customer inventories improved (A, B). Lower server demand, weaker external foundry sales and Altera customers cutting purchases (C–E) could pull total growth to -5% in Q3 or Q4 if the client rebound fades.

Amkor’s Q2 net sales recovered to +0.24% from -7.21% in Q1 because communications growth offset declines elsewhere (A). Elevated customer inventories and weaker demand drove first-half declines of 19% in automotive and industrial and 12% in consumer (B). A smaller communications offset could put Q3 or Q4 back at or below -5%.

ArcBest’s consolidated revenue improved from -6.30% in Q1 to -2.32% in Q2 (A). It still faced lower Asset-Light freight rates and lower Asset-Based daily tonnage (B). Further weakness in rates or tonnage could erase the 2.68-point cushion in Q3 or Q4.
